key_insight: This paper shows that multimodal LLMs can run faster by jointly deciding both what visual tokens to keep and how much language-model computation to use. Instead of optimizing token reduction and compute reduction separately, the authors adapt them together for better efficiency with less accuracy loss.
problem_solved: Multimodal LLMs are expensive to deploy because they process many visual tokens and require heavy language-model computation. Existing methods usually reduce only one of these costs at a time, missing opportunities for more efficient joint optimization.
method: Jointly adapts visual token usage and LLM computation during inference rather than treating them as separate problems.
Removes or downweights redundant visual tokens to reduce input size.
Skips or reduces unnecessary LLM computation, such as layers or heads, to lower inference cost.
impact: This makes multimodal AI systems more practical for real-world deployment by cutting latency and compute cost while preserving performance. It is especially useful for edge devices, high-throughput services, and cost-sensitive applications.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline diagram showing many visual tokens vs. pruned tokens
Compute budget chart comparing baseline, token-only, compute-only, and joint adaptation
Icon-based flow showing image encoder, token pruning, and LLM skipping
Accuracy-vs-latency tradeoff curve highlighting the efficiency gains
paper_title: Look Less, Think Faster: Joint Token-Compute Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs
paper_authors: Pengcheng Wang, Zhiquan Wang, Jayoung Lee, Zhuoyan Xu, Ran Xu
